short: A converted battlecruiser, Akagi served as the flagship of the Japanese First Air Fleet before being sunk at Midway.
full:
Originally laid down as an Amagi-class battlecruiser, Akagi was converted into an aircraft carrier and commissioned in 1927. As one of the Imperial Japanese Navy's most experienced carriers, she was at the forefront of naval aviation doctrine. She served as the flagship of Vice Admiral Chuichi Nagumo during the devastating surprise attack on Pearl Harbor in December 1941, launching a wave of destruction against the American Pacific Fleet.

Akagi subsequently projected Japanese power across the Pacific and into the Indian Ocean. In June 1942, during the pivotal Battle of Midway, American dive bombers caught her flight deck full of armed and fueled aircraft. A single bomb strike triggered massive secondary explosions, dooming the ship and dealing a fatal blow to Japanese naval supremacy.
